subject: Technical qualification: function-calling & deterministic JSON output requirements
body:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@finovate.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Technical qualification: function-calling & deterministic JSON output requirements

Dana —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side so we all have the same picture and the right folks lined up for the technical deep dive. I’ve split this into pain, current stack, success criteria, and immediate next steps so it’s actionable.

Pain points we heard
- Post-processing cost & brittleness: Your ingestion team spends ~40% of time on parsing and mapping model output into downstream systems when responses are inconsistent.
- Agent orchestration gaps: You run a multi-step agent workflow (retrieval -> tool call -> commit) and need stronger guarantees around deterministic tool outputs so downstream systems don’t break.
- Security & audit: You need evidence of structured outputs, immutable logs, and schema validation for compliance.

Current stack (as you described)
- Frontend: React + FastAPI proxy
- Orchestration: A lightweight in-house agent manager that coordinates tools (search, ticketing API, billing API)
- Models: Mix of open models hosted on cloud VMs; some heavy post-processing in Python to normalize outputs
- Observability: ELK stack; no token-level tracing today (manual correlation)

Success criteria (what success looks like for Finovate)
- JSON-first responses: >=95% of model responses conform to a provided JSON schema with clear validation errors (not free-form text).
- Reliable tool/function calls: Agent tool outputs are deterministic and annotated so they can be replayed and audited.
- End-to-end latency <= 400ms median for happy-path calls (when using our dedicated routing).
- Demonstrable audit trail: signed, timestamped logs for each request and function-call event.

Technical priorities we’ll focus on in the next call
1) Schema design: We’ll review your example event types and map them to a minimal, strongly-typed JSON schema (we’ve attached a Redwood JSON schema template).
2) Function/tool calling contract: Define the precise function signatures and success/failure modes for each tool the agent will call (idempotency, retry semantics, and error envelopes).
3) Determinism checks: Propose a regression test harness that runs prompt+input permutations and checks JSON conformance and token-level diffs.
4) Observability hooks: Outline required traces/log fields so your ELK stack can ingest token costs, function-call events, and schema validation results.

Action items / next steps
- Dana / Jamal: please share two example user prompts + expected JSON payloads and your current mapping script for one workflow by EOD Wed 5/20. (attachment: finovate-current-stack.pdf was helpful; please add the sample prompts there).
- Finovate security: please confirm NDA/POC security checklist items you need before a private deployment (cc’d security@finovate.ai).
- Redwood: Rishi will join the technical deep dive to walk through schema mapping and runtime guarantees. Proposed time: Thu 5/21 10:00–11:00 PT. I’ve attached a proposed technical agenda.

Attachment references:
- redwood-json-schema-template.json (starter schema + examples)
- proposed-technical-agenda.docx (30m deep-dive + 30m hands-on testing)
- finovate-current-stack.pdf (shared by Jamal)

If that aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite with the agenda and a short pre-read.

Thanks — and happy to adapt if I missed anything.

—
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
